Position: Motor Mechanic
Type: Full-time
Employer: Unique Collision Pty Ltd
Location: Huntingdale VIC 3166
Salary: $100,000 p/a
About the Business:
Unique Collision Pty Ltd is a reputable panel beating and collision repair business based in Huntingdale, Victoria, serving the greater Melbourne area. We specialise in comprehensive vehicle repair and restoration services, including insurance claims management, private work, full detailing, paintless dent removal, replacement vehicles, and free pick-up and delivery. Committed to delivering high-quality premium service, we pride ourselves on exceptional workmanship, customer satisfaction, and a supportive, team-oriented workplace culture where attention to detail and professionalism are valued.
About the Position:
As a Motor Mechanic at Unique Collision Pty Ltd, you will play a vital role in diagnosing, repairing, and maintaining vehicles to the highest standards following collision repairs and mechanical issues. This full-time position involves a broad scope of mechanical work to ensure vehicles are safe, reliable, and returned to customers in excellent condition, supporting the business’s commitment to premium service and operational efficiency in our busy collision repair workshop.
Key Responsibilities:
Diagnose mechanical and electrical faults in engines and vehicle components.
Dismantle and remove engine assemblies, transmissions, steering mechanisms, and other parts, inspecting and checking them for defects.
Repair and replace worn or defective parts, reassemble mechanical components, and refer to service manuals as required.
Perform vehicle paint preparation, mechanical repairs, and scheduled maintenance services such as oil changes and tune-ups.
Conduct final inspections, quality control checks, and testing of repaired vehicles to ensure proper performance and compliance with standards.
Dismantle and assemble vehicles as needed to support panel beating and collision repair processes.
Requirements:
Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.
Certificate III in relevant automotive or mechanical qualifications.
At least 2 years of industry experience as a Motor Mechanic.
Strong technical skills in diagnosing faults, mechanical repairs, electrical systems, and vehicle assembly/disassembly.
Excellent attention to detail, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to high-quality workmanship.
Good interpersonal skills with the ability to work effectively as part of a team in a fast-paced workshop environment.
How to Apply:
To apply, applicants must submit their resume with a valid email address through this online portal.
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Payroll Officer – Full-Time
Location: Welshpool, Western Australia 6106
Employment Type: Full-Time
Salary: $75,000 – $90,000 per annum (depending on skills and experience)

MINPROVISE INTERNATIONAL PTY LTD is a leading total solutions provider delivering specialist maintenance and shutdown services, engineering, fabrication, project services, and sustaining capital works. We also provide a comprehensive range of equipment and products, supporting the mining, oil & gas, and construction industries across Australia and internationally.

We are currently seeking an experienced and detail-oriented Payroll Officer to join our growing team on a full-time basis.

About the Role
As a Payroll Officer, you will be responsible for managing payroll processing activities, maintaining accurate employee records, and ensuring employees are paid correctly and on time. You will work closely with the finance, human resources, project, and operational teams to ensure payroll processes comply with company policies, awards, employment conditions, and relevant legislation.

Key Responsibilities
•	Process end-to-end payroll activities for employees, including weekly and fortnightly payroll cycles.
•	Maintain accurate employee payroll records, including salaries, allowances, deductions, leave balances, and employment details.
•	Verify timesheets, overtime, allowances, leave applications, and payroll adjustments.
•	Ensure payroll calculations comply with relevant awards, enterprise agreements, employment contracts, and legislation.
•	Process new employee onboarding, payroll setup, and employee changes.
•	Manage employee queries relating to payroll, leave entitlements, deductions, and payments.
•	Prepare payroll reports, reconciliations, and supporting documentation for management and finance teams.
•	Process superannuation payments, payroll tax, PAYG withholding, and other statutory obligations.
•	Maintain accurate records and assist with payroll audits and compliance reviews.
•	Liaise with HR, project managers, supervisors, and employees regarding payroll-related matters.
•	Assist with improving payroll processes and maintaining payroll system accuracy.
•	Ensure confidentiality and security of employee payroll information.
•	Follow workplace health and safety policies, company procedures, and quality management systems.

Skills and Experience
•	Minimum 1–2 years of full-time experience as a Payroll Officer or in a similar payroll/finance administration role.
•	Experience processing payroll in a medium to large organisation is highly regarded.
•	Strong understanding of payroll processes, employment conditions, and statutory requirements.
•	Experience with payroll software and Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel.
•	Strong attention to detail and accuracy in handling financial and employee data.
•	Excellent organisational and time management skills.
•	Ability to manage confidential information professionally.
•	Strong communication skills and ability to work effectively with employees and management teams.

What We Offer
•	Full-time, permanent employment.
•	Competitive salary of $75,000 – $90,000 per annum.
•	Opportunities to work within a growing mining and industrial services organisation.
•	Ongoing training and professional development.
•	Supportive team environment with long-term career opportunities.

We are currently seeking experienced and motivated Advanced Scaffolders / Scaffolders to join our growing team on a full-time basis.

About the Role

You will work closely with supervisors and project teams to ensure all scaffolding is installed safely, efficiently, and in compliance with Australian Standards and workplace safety requirements.

Key Responsibilities
•	Read and interpret scaffolding plans, drawings, and specifications.
•	Erect, alter, inspect, and dismantle scaffolding systems for commercial, industrial, and mining projects.
•	Ensure scaffolding structures are safe, secure, and compliant with Australian Standards and site requirements.
•	Install edge protection, temporary access platforms, stair systems, handrails, and safety barriers.
•	Conduct routine inspections of scaffolding and identify defects or maintenance requirements.
•	Load, unload, transport, and organise scaffolding materials and equipment.

Overview:

UON is a Western Australian integrated energy company providing turnkey energy and water solutions to the
mining sector and beyond. Central to this is helping our customers on their decarbonisation journey utilising
the technology, skills and real experience of team members across the business.

UON’s business centres around the design, manufacturing, supply, construction and maintenance of remote,
off-grid power and water infrastructure, with many of the products manufactured in UON’s Malaga facility,
based on proprietary and patented designs.

We are seeking an experienced Purchasing Manager to join our team in Malaga, WA. In this role, you will be
responsible for planning, directing and coordinating procurement and purchasing activities to ensure the
efficient acquisition of materials, products and services required to support business operations. This is a fulltime
ongoing position working 38 hours per week.


Main tasks:

- Determining, implementing and monitoring procurement and purchasing strategies, policies and plans
to support organisational objectives.
- Negotiating and managing supplier contracts to achieve quality, cost and delivery requirements.
- Developing and maintaining supplier relationships to ensure continuity of supply and optimal
commercial outcomes.
- Monitoring procurement activities and purchasing processes to ensure compliance with company
policies and operational requirements.
- Preparing and implementing inventory management plans to maintain required stock levels while
minimising costs.
- Reviewing and monitoring storage and inventory control systems to ensure efficient stock management
and supply availability.
- Overseeing purchasing and inventory recording systems to ensure accurate tracking of materials,
supplies and finished goods.
- Analysing purchasing trends, supplier performance and market conditions to identify opportunities for
cost savings and operational improvements.
- Liaising with internal stakeholders to identify procurement requirements and ensure timely supply of
products and services.
- Coordinating procurement activities associated with transportation, logistics and distribution
requirements.
- Directing and supervising procurement staff, allocating duties and monitoring performance against
established objectives.
- Ensuring purchasing activities support operational efficiency, project requirements and customer
expectations.
- Preparing procurement reports, forecasts, budgets and recommendations for management.
- Performing any additional duties as required from time to time. Perform any additional tasks as
required from time to time.


Required/Relevant Qualifications & Work Experience:

- Bachelor’s degree (or higher qualification) in Supply Chain Management, Business, Commerce,
Procurement, Logistics or a related discipline.
- Alternatively, at least five years of relevant procurement, purchasing or supply chain management
experience may substitute for the formal qualification.


Required/Relevant Skills & Knowledge:

- Strong contract negotiation and supplier relationship management skills
- Demonstrated experience in procurement planning, supplier management, contract negotiation and
inventory control
- Experience working within a medium to large organisation managing procurement functions and
purchasing operations.
- Ability to develop and implement procurement strategies, policies and procedures.
- Sound knowledge of purchasing, inventory management and stock control systems.
- Strong analytical, commercial and problem-solving skills.
- Ability to assess supplier performance and identify cost optimisation opportunities
- Excellent organisational and time management skills.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
- Strong leadership and people management capabilities.
- High attention to detail and accuracy
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and procurement management systems
- Ability to build and maintain effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders.


Annual salary will be between $100,000.00 to $120,000.00 (plus superannuation) depending on level of
experience.

Greenwood Leather is a proudly Australian, family-run maker of fine leather bags and accessories. Since 2016 we have followed a simple passion to craft leather pieces that people genuinely love. Every wallet, handbag and travel bag is handmade and one of a kind, blending old-world craftsmanship with fresh, considered design. Our products are made from the heart, and each carries its own name. Together they form “families” of designs meant to be companions for life pieces that soften, age and gain character with everyday use, gathering the stories of the journeys and people they travel with. Choosing a Greenwood piece means joining our family: customers who value quality over passing trends and who have a soft spot for individual, unconventional style. Based in Cranbourne West, Victoria, we are a growing brand with big ambitions for how our story reaches the people who will love it. That is where you come in.

Key Responsibilities
•	Plan and carry out market research and brief external specialists where needed to uncover fresh opportunities for both our established bag families and any new pieces or accessories we are considering.
•	Study buyer demand and the wider leather-goods and fashion market, gathering and interpreting sales figures, customer data and other statistics to guide where the brand heads next.
•	Guide decisions across the full marketing mix our product range, pricing, promotions and advertising, sales activity, and the retail and online channels through which our products reach customers.
•	Help drive the growth of the business by shaping, documenting and delivering clear marketing objectives, plans and programs, and tracking how well they perform against our goals.
•	Translate customer and market insight into positioning and messaging that stays true to Greenwood’s handcrafted, story-led identity.
•	Develop and manage campaigns across our website, email, social media and other digital channels to build brand awareness and lift online and in-store sales.
•	Monitor competitors, seasonal trends and emerging channels, and recommend practical ways for Greenwood to respond and stand out.
•	Work closely with the design and production side of the business so that marketing activity reflects the true craftsmanship and unique character of each product.
•	Measure the results of marketing spend and report on performance, using what we learn to sharpen future activity and improve return on investment.
•	Support the customer experience from launches and content to promotions and events so that every touchpoint reinforces the feeling of joining the Greenwood family.

What You’ll Bring
•	A Bachelor degree or higher qualification (AQF level 7 or above) in marketing, business, communications or a related field.
•	At least one year of relevant experience in a marketing role.

Personal Attributes
•	Creative and curious you enjoy finding new angles and telling a story well.
•	Organised and self-motivated, able to juggle several projects and meet deadlines.
•	A natural collaborator who works warmly with a small, tight team.
•	Detail-oriented, with pride in doing things properly.
•	Adaptable and hands-on, happy to roll up your sleeves in a growing business.
•	Aligned with our values authenticity, craftsmanship and individuality over chasing every trend.

Hours, Pay & How to Apply:

Employment type: Full-time, approximately 38 hours per week.

Salary:  $95,000 – $105,000 per annum, plus superannuation.

Location: Cranbourne West, VIC.

If you love the idea of helping a heartfelt Australian brand grow, we would love to hear from you. Please submit your resume and a short cover letter telling us why Greenwood Leather is the right fit for you.

About Burlington Berries
Burlington Berries is a leading berry production company located in the fertile Northern Midlands of Tasmania. Known for delivering high-quality strawberries, raspberries, and blackberries to major national retailers, Burlington Berries combines innovative growing techniques with sustainable farming practices. Our operations combine leading horticultural practices with a strong commitment to sustainability, innovation, and excellence in every stage of berry production. Our team is passionate about excellence in horticulture and dedicated to producing premium fresh produce for Australian consumers.

Position Overview
The full-time Irrigationist Assitant supports the planning, maintenance, and execution of irrigation systems across Burlington Berries’ production areas. Working under the direction of the Irrigationist, this role is hands-on and operationally focused, ensuring that all irrigation tasks are carried out accurately, efficiently, and in a timely manner. The role is ideal for someone looking to grow their technical skills in a fast-paced, high-yield berry farming environment.

Key Responsibilities/Tasks
Irrigation Support and Execution
•	Assist in daily irrigation operations including the setup, adjustment, and monitoring of drip lines, valves, and other water delivery infrastructure.
•	Execute irrigation schedules as directed, ensuring water application matches crop requirements across different berry varieties and stages of growth.
•	Observing the crop daily to ensure optimal fertigation programs

System Checks and Maintenance
•	Conduct routine inspections of irrigation systems to identify leaks, clogs, or wear-and-tear on components.
•	Support filter cleaning, emitter flushing, pressure checks, and other maintenance activities to ensure optimal system performance.

Data Logging and Communication
•	Record irrigation and fertigation activities as required, including volumes applied, timing, and any system faults.
•	Recording  water and fertiliser use and report on for each crop type
•	Communicate effectively with supervisors, agronomists, and other team members regarding field conditions, task completion, and issues requiring escalation.
•	Attending daily meetings to help align the irrigation/fertigation plans with the daily climatic changes and crop requirements

Infrastructure Installation and Upgrades
•	Assist with installation and modification of irrigation lines, control valves, filters, and pumps for new planting blocks or seasonal adjustments.
•	Work alongside contractors or in-house teams during major system upgrades or expansions.

Fertigation and Nutrient Delivery
•	Prepare and apply fertigation mixes under guidance, ensuring accurate dosing through injection systems.
•	Monitor fertigation equipment during runs and report any issues or anomalies promptly.

Key Skills and Attributes
•	Willingness to learn and apply technical irrigation and fertigation skills in a commercial horticulture setting.
•	Good attention to detail, especially when working with measurement, timing, and calibration tasks.
•	Reliability and a strong work ethic, including availability for early starts, weekends, and peak seasonal periods.
•	Ability to follow instructions, take initiative, and work safely in outdoor environments.
•	Interest in agriculture, irrigation, or horticulture as a career path.

Qualifications and Experience
•	A basic understanding of irrigation systems, pumps, and fertigation principles is an advantage.
•	Certificate II or III in Agriculture, Irrigation, or Horticulture and one year of work experience (at least 20+hrs per week), or have at least 2 years full time work experience in lieu of formal qualifications
•	Current driver’s licence required; machinery tickets (e.g., forklift, quad bike) are beneficial but not essential.

Salary
.       $72,000-$81,000 + Superannuation depending on experience

To ensure clinical efficiency, the GP is supported by an experienced nursing and administrative team, dedicated Chronic Disease Management (CDM) support, onsite pathology, and integrated allied health services. 

 Operating as a bulk billing clinic, the practice provides a competitive remuneration package of 65% to 75% of billings alongside a minimum income guarantee to ensure a smooth transition. The incoming GP will inherit a robust, established patient base of 40 to 50 patients per day while enjoying full clinical autonomy. The clinic offers unique opportunities for practitioners to engage in special interest areas, such as micro-needling treatments and Platelet-Rich Plasma (PRP) injections. Recognizing the importance of work-life balance, the practice offers significant flexible working arrangements, including options for remote access. For those looking to expand their professional horizons, there are also opportunities for CPD support and to step into supervisor roles. 

 Located in an MM1 region, this role is suitable for both permanent placements and long-term locums. Beyond the clinic walls, Carnes Hill offers an enviable lifestyle in a vibrant community known for its modern housing and excellent community facilities. The practice is conveniently situated within Carnes Hill Market Place, offering easy access to public transport and being only a 20-minute drive from Liverpool Hospital. With proximity to the Western Sydney University Liverpool campus and the nearby Liverpool train station, it is the perfect destination for a practitioner seeking professional financial success and clinical variety in a well-connected Sydney suburb. Location: Munglinup, WA, 6450
Full-Time: Immediate start
Reports to: Manager
Job Title: Agricultural and Horticultural Mobile Plant Operator
Salary range: $79,500 - $85,000 + Superannuation - Overtime and Penalty Rates are also available. Depending on skill level and suitability
Job Closure date: 30 days

About The Role
We are seeking an experienced Agricultural & Horticultural Mobile Plant Operator to join a large-scale, progressive farming enterprise in Western Australia. This role is critical to supporting a mixed farming operation that includes broadacre cropping, livestock production, and emerging horticultural and tree crop initiatives. The successful candidate will operate a variety of mobile plant machinery across multiple properties, contributing to sustainable land management and efficient farm operations.
This position is ideal for a skilled operator who is mechanically minded, safety-focused, and comfortable working across diverse agricultural settings—from cropping paddocks to livestock stations. You will play a key role in maintaining and optimising farm productivity while adhering to regenerative farming principles.

Key Responsibilities:
Machine Operation & Site Work:
• Safely transport and operate mobile plant machinery (e.g., tractors, loaders, excavators, spray rigs) across broadacre cropping, livestock, and horticultural sites.
• Manoeuvre equipment efficiently in varied terrain, including paddocks, irrigation zones, and newly developed horticultural blocks.
• Assist with land preparation, seeding, fertiliser application, and crop maintenance in alignment with sustainable farming practices.

Attachment Handling & Precision Work:
• Select, fit, and operate specialised attachments (e.g., slashers, seeder, front-end loaders, post drivers) for tasks such as feed preparation, fencing, and soil conditioning.
• Adjust hydraulic, mechanical, and electronic controls to ensure precise operation of implements—critical for tasks like controlled traffic farming (CTF) and pasture renovation.
• Support livestock operations by handling hay baling, silage compaction, and feed-out machinery.

Equipment Monitoring & Maintenance:
• Conduct pre-start checks, monitor gauges/telematics, and perform routine servicing (e.g., greasing, fluid top-ups, filter changes) to maintain machinery performance.
• Diagnose minor mechanical issues, carry out basic repairs, and report major faults to maintenance teams promptly.
• Ensure compliance with safety standards and manufacturer guidelines for all equipment.

Team Collaboration & Autonomous Work:
• Coordinate with farm supervisors, agronomists, and livestock teams to prioritise tasks such as irrigation, weed control, or infrastructure projects.
• Work independently during remote operations (e.g., fence-line repairs, paddock grading) while maintaining clear communication with managers.
• Participate in seasonal projects, including potential horticultural expansion (e.g., orchard establishment, vineyard development).

Essential Requirements:
• Relevant Qualification + minimum 1 year of full-time experience operating mobile plant in farming environments.
• Proficiency with tractors, loaders, and attachments; familiarity with precision agriculture tools (e.g., GPS guidance) is advantageous.
• Strong adherence to WorkSafe standards and farm-specific safety protocols.
Reliable, self-motivated, and capable of working long hours during peak seasons (e.g., harvest, seeding).
• Willingness to contribute to a collaborative farming operation with a focus on regenerative agriculture and land stewardship.

Desirable Attributes:
• Experience in broadacre cropping (wheat, barley, canola) or livestock support operations (feed logistics, pasture management).
• Exposure to horticultural machinery (e.g., vine pruners, harvesters) or interest in diversifying into tree crops.
• HR/MR truck licence (for machinery relocation between properties).

Why Apply?
• Join a forward-thinking enterprise investing in sustainable land use and diversified farming systems.
• Varied role spanning cropping, livestock, and emerging horticulture—no two days are the same!

How to Apply:
Submit your resume and a brief cover letter outlining your machinery experience and suitability for mixed farming operations.

Position Title: Fleet Manager
Employment Type: 38 Hours a week minimum, Full-Time, Permanent 
Salary Range: $90,000 – $110,000 per annum plus superannuation
Location: Office Suite 4, 66 Commercial Drive Shailer Park QLD 4128

About the role 
We are seeking an experienced and highly organised Fleet Manager to oversee and coordinate the efficient operation of transport fleet for our client SODHI SERVICES PTY LTD. Our client has successful transportation business and has fleets including multiple trucks and trailers. They are adding more vehicles and requires a full-time dedicated fleet manager to manage the operations. The successful candidate will be responsible for managing fleet performance, vehicle utilisation, driver coordination, maintenance planning, and compliance requirements to ensure safe, reliable, and cost-effective transport operations. This role requires strong leadership skills, operational knowledge, and the ability to optimise fleet resources while maintaining high standards of safety, productivity, and service delivery.

Key Duties 
•	Manage and coordinate daily fleet operations, ensuring vehicles are efficiently allocated and available to meet business and customer delivery requirements.
•	Develop and implement fleet management strategies to improve vehicle utilisation, operational efficiency, cost control, and overall transport performance.
•	Monitor fleet schedules, vehicle availability, and operational requirements to support timely delivery services and minimise disruptions.
•	Coordinate regular vehicle servicing, inspections, repairs, and maintenance activities in collaboration with workshops and service providers.
•	Maintain accurate fleet records, including vehicle registrations, maintenance history, compliance documentation, and operational reports.
•	Supervise and support drivers, ensuring adherence to company procedures, workplace health and safety requirements, and transport regulations.
•	Review driver performance, provide operational guidance, and promote safe driving practices and responsible vehicle use.
•	Monitor fuel consumption, vehicle operating costs, and fleet expenses to identify opportunities for improved efficiency and cost reduction.
•	Ensure compliance with relevant transport legislation, heavy vehicle requirements, road safety standards, and company policies.
•	Coordinate vehicle procurement, replacement planning, and disposal processes to maintain an effective and reliable fleet.
•	Analyse fleet performance data, prepare operational reports, and provide recommendations to management for continuous improvement.
•	Manage relationships with external suppliers, mechanics, contractors, and service providers to ensure quality fleet support services.
•	Implement risk management procedures, including safety inspections, incident reporting, and corrective actions to improve fleet reliability.
•	Assist with route efficiency reviews and operational planning to maximise productivity and customer service outcomes.

Qualification and Experience Requirement. 
•	Minimum comparable Diploma or higher AQF level 
•	Highly relevant minimum 1 year of employment experience 

Skills and Attributes
•	Strong understanding of fleet operations, vehicle management, and transport compliance requirements.
•	Excellent organisational and problem-solving abilities.
•	Ability to coordinate multiple operational priorities in a fast-paced environment.
•	Strong communication and leadership skills to manage drivers and operational stakeholders.
•	Sound knowledge of safety procedures, maintenance scheduling, and cost management practices.

Remuneration
The successful candidate will receive an annual salary between $90,000 and $110,000 plus superannuation, commensurate with skills, experience, and industry standards.

Application duration: 28 July 2026 to 27 August 2026.  Kindly apply with your resume and you will be contacted if shortlisted for the interview.
